   290→### 4. Full pipeline: implement → smoke test → PR → simplify → review loop
   291→
   292→The full pattern matching `dev-loop.py`'s battle-tested pipeline. Applies all six context patterns above.
   293→
   294→```python
   295→import subprocess, time
   296→
   297→# --- Implementation ---
   298→graph.add_node("implement", claude_node(
   299→    "You are working in {work_dir}. Read the plan at {plan_path} and implement it.\n\n"
   300→    "After completing all tasks:\n"
   301→    "1. Update documentation (README, docstrings, diagrams) to reflect changes\n"
   302→    "2. Run the project's quality gates (lint, typecheck, format, tests)\n"
   303→    "Fix any failures before proceeding.",
   304→    output_key="impl_output", model="opus", effort="high",
   305→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   306→))
   307→
   308→# --- Smoke test (context pattern 6) ---
   309→graph.add_node("smoke_test", claude_node(
   310→    "You are working in {work_dir}. Run a smoke test to verify the implementation.\n\n"
   311→    "1. Read the plan at {plan_path}. Look for a '## Validation' section.\n"
   312→    "2. If found, execute those validation instructions exactly.\n"
   313→    "3. If NOT found, fall back to convention-based discovery:\n"
   314→    "   - Read README.md, pyproject.toml, package.json, Makefile, docker-compose.yml\n"
   315→    "   - Run a basic sanity check (does it start? does --help work?)\n"
   316→    "4. ALWAYS kill all background processes before finishing.\n\n"
   317→    "End with EXACTLY one line:\n"
   318→    "  SMOKE_TEST_PASS\n"
   319→    "  SMOKE_TEST_FAIL: <brief summary>",
   320→    output_key="smoke_test_output", model="opus", effort="high",
   321→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   322→))
   323→
   324→graph.add_node("smoke_test_fix", claude_node(
   325→    "You are working in {work_dir}. The smoke test failed:\n\n{smoke_test_output}\n\n"
   326→    "Diagnose the root cause, fix the code, then run quality gates "
   327→    "(lint, typecheck, format, tests). Commit fixes locally.",
   328→    output_key="smoke_test_fix_output", model="opus", effort="high",
   329→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   330→))
   331→
   332→# No separate retry node — smoke_test_fix loops back to smoke_test.
   333→# If the smoke test fails a second time, max_iterations will stop the loop.
   334→
   335→# --- PR creation ---
   336→graph.add_node("create_pr", claude_node(
   337→    "You are working in {work_dir}. Push the current branch and create a PR:\n"
   338→    "  git push -u origin HEAD\n"
   339→    "  gh pr create --title '<descriptive title>' --body '<summary of changes>'\n\n"
   340→    "Return the PR URL.",
   341→    output_key="pr_url", model="sonnet", effort="low",
   342→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   343→))
   344→
   345→# --- Simplify ---
   346→graph.add_node("simplify", claude_node(
   347→    "/simplify",
   348→    output_key="simplify_output", model="sonnet", effort="high",
   349→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   350→))
   351→
   352→graph.add_node("simplify_commit", claude_node(
   353→    "If there are any uncommitted changes from the simplify pass, "
   354→    "commit them with a descriptive message and push to the current branch.",
   355→    output_key="simplify_commit_output", model="sonnet", effort="low",
   356→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   357→))
   358→
   359→# --- Parallel reviews (context patterns 1, 2, 3) ---
   360→graph.add_node("code_review", claude_node(
   361→    "/code-review:code-review {pr_url}",
   362→    output_key="code_review_output", model="opus", effort="high",
   363→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   364→))
   365→
   366→graph.add_node("security_review", claude_node(
   367→    "/security-review\n\n"
   368→    "Review the changes in PR {pr_url}.\n\n"
   369→    "IMPORTANT: A previous security review found these issues. "
   370→    "Check if they are resolved AND do a full new review "
   371→    "(fixes may introduce new issues):\n\n"
   372→    "{previous_security_findings}\n\n"
   373→    "After completing the review, post findings as a PR comment:\n"
   374→    "  gh pr comment <pr_number> --body '<findings>'\n\n"
   375→    "Format with a '### Security Review' header and severity categories.",
   376→    output_key="security_review_output", model="opus", effort="high",
   377→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   378→))
   379→
   380→# --- Wait for CI ---
   381→def _wait_for_ci_fn(state: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
   382→    """Poll CI checks until complete. Returns ci_status and ci_failures."""
   383→    pr_url = state.get("pr_url", "")
   384→    pr_number = pr_url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1] if pr_url else ""
   385→    max_wait = 600  # 10 minutes
   386→    start = time.monotonic()
   387→    while time.monotonic() - start < max_wait:
   388→        result = subprocess.run(
   389→            ["gh", "pr", "checks", pr_number, "--json", "name,state,conclusion"],
   390→            capture_output=True, text=True,
   391→        )
   392→        if result.returncode != 0:
   393→            return {"ci_status": "pass", "ci_failures": ""}
   394→        output = result.stdout
   395→        if '"pending"' not in output.lower() and '"queued"' not in output.lower():
   396→            if '"failure"' in output.lower() or '"error"' in output.lower():
   397→                return {"ci_status": "fail", "ci_failures": output}
   398→            return {"ci_status": "pass", "ci_failures": ""}
   399→        time.sleep(30)
   400→    return {"ci_status": "pass", "ci_failures": ""}  # timeout = assume pass
   401→
   402→graph.add_node("wait_for_ci", python_node(_wait_for_ci_fn))
   403→
   404→# --- Decision gate (context pattern 4) ---
   405→def _decision_fn(state: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
   406→    """Evaluate reviews + CI. Carry previous_security_findings, increment iteration.
   407→
   408→    This is a python_node wrapper around the LLM decision so we can also
   409→    carry state (previous_security_findings) and short-circuit on CI failure.
   410→    Note: the LLM (decision_llm) always runs before this node in the graph.
   411→    In dev-loop.py, the decision node conditionally skips the LLM call on CI
   412→    failure — this two-node split is a simplification for the example.
   413→    """
   414→    ci_status = state.get("ci_status", "pass")
   415→    security_text = state.get("security_review_output", "")
   416→    iteration = int(state.get("iteration_count", "1"))
   417→
   418→    if ci_status == "fail":
   419→        return {
   420→            "decision_output": "YES",
   421→            "previous_security_findings": security_text,
   422→            "iteration_count": str(iteration + 1),
   423→        }
   424→
   425→    return {
   426→        "decision_output": state.get("decision_llm_output", "NO"),
   427→        "previous_security_findings": security_text,
   428→        "iteration_count": str(iteration + 1),
   429→    }
   430→
   431→graph.add_node("decision_llm", claude_node(
   432→    "Based on these review findings, are there Critical, Important, or Medium "
   433→    "severity issues that MUST be fixed?\n\n"
   434→    "Code Review:\n{code_review_output}\n\n"
   435→    "Security Review:\n{security_review_output}\n\n"
   436→    "CI failures:\n{ci_failures}\n\n"
   437→    "Answer EXACTLY: YES or NO. Only YES for Critical/Important/Medium issues "
   438→    "or CI failures. Low severity and nitpicks do not count.",
   439→    output_key="decision_llm_output", model="sonnet", effort="low",
   440→))
   441→graph.add_node("decision", python_node(_decision_fn))
   442→
   443→# --- Fix (context pattern 5) ---
   444→graph.add_node("fix", claude_node(
   445→    "Fix all Critical, Important, and Medium severity issues from this review "
   446→    "of PR {pr_url}.\n\n"
   447→    "Code Review:\n{code_review_output}\n\n"
   448→    "Security Review:\n{security_review_output}\n\n"
   449→    "CI failures:\n{ci_failures}\n\n"
   450→    "After fixing, run quality gates (lint, typecheck, format, tests). "
   451→    "Fix any failures. Commit and push.",
   452→    output_key="fix_output", model="opus", effort="high",
   453→    permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
   454→))
   455→
   456→# --- Routers ---
   457→def smoke_test_router(state: dict[str, str]) -> str:
   458→    error = state.get("smoke_test_error", "")
   459→    output = state.get("smoke_test_output", "")
   460→    if error or "SMOKE_TEST_FAIL" in output:
   461→        return "fail"
   462→    return "pass"
   463→
   464→def decision_router(state: dict[str, str]) -> str:
   465→    if "YES" in state.get("decision_output", "NO").upper():
   466→        return "fix"
   467→    return "done"

   470→# Phase 1: implement → smoke test → PR
   471→graph.add_edge("start", "implement")
   472→graph.add_edge("implement", "smoke_test")
   473→graph.add_conditional_edges("smoke_test", smoke_test_router, {
   474→    "pass": "create_pr", "fail": "smoke_test_fix",

   476→graph.add_edge("smoke_test_fix", "smoke_test")  # retry by re-entering smoke_test

   479→graph.add_edge("create_pr", "simplify")
   480→graph.add_edge("simplify", "simplify_commit")
   481→graph.add_parallel_edges("simplify_commit", ["code_review", "security_review"])
   482→graph.add_edge("code_review", "wait_for_ci")
   483→graph.add_edge("security_review", "wait_for_ci")
   484→graph.add_edge("wait_for_ci", "decision_llm")
   485→graph.add_edge("decision_llm", "decision")
   486→graph.add_conditional_edges("decision", decision_router, {"fix": "fix", "done": END})
   487→graph.add_edge("fix", "simplify")  # loop back to review
   488→```
   489→
   490→## Important rules
   491→
   492→- **Fail fast.** Don't add retries to nodes. If you need retry logic, build it as a loop in the graph (conditional edge back to a fix node).
   493→- **State is strings.** All state values are strings. Use `python_node` to parse or transform if needed.
   494→- **Set max_iterations.** Always set a reasonable `max_iterations` to prevent infinite loops. Default is 5.
   495→- **Right-size the model.** Use `HAS_CODEX`/`HAS_GEMINI` from `detect_available_models()` to pick the best available tool for each step. Use Codex for code gen, Gemini for text tasks, and Claude when you need codebase navigation or deep reasoning. See the model selection guide above.
   496→- **Permission mode.** For Claude nodes that need to edit files, set `permission_mode="bypassPermissions"` for headless execution.
   497→- **Always commit at the end.** If the workflow modifies code, add a final `shell_node` that commits and pushes the changes.
   498→- **Safe commits.** Use `git diff --cached --quiet && echo "nothing to commit" || git commit -m "..."` to handle cases where there's nothing to commit.
   499→- **Working directory in prompts.** Always include `You are working in {work_dir}` in Claude node prompts so headless sessions know where to find files.
   500→- **Parallel reviews need a fan-out node.** Use a passthrough `python_node(lambda s: {})` before `add_parallel_edges` since conditional and parallel edges on the same node conflict.

   194→def create_github_repo(project_dir: Path, repo_name: str) -> str:
   195→    """Initialize git, create GitHub repo, push. Returns OWNER/REPO."""
   196→    subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=project_dir, capture_output=True)
   197→    subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", "-b", "main"], cwd=project_dir, capture_output=True)
   198→    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=project_dir, capture_output=True)
   199→    subprocess.run(
   200→        ["git", "commit", "-m", "Initial commit: basic calculator"],
   201→        cwd=project_dir,
   202→        capture_output=True,
   203→    )
   204→    result = subprocess.run(
   205→        ["gh", "repo", "create", repo_name, "--private", "--source=.", "--push"],
   206→        cwd=project_dir,
   207→        capture_output=True,
   208→        text=True,
   209→        timeout=30,
   210→    )
   211→    if result.returncode != 0:
   212→        print(f"Failed to create GitHub repo: {result.stderr}", file=sys.stderr)
   213→        sys.exit(1)
   214→    # Extract owner/repo from the first line of stdout (URL like https://github.com/owner/repo)

   216→    repo_url = result.stdout.strip().splitlines()[0].strip()
   217→    parts = repo_url.rstrip("/").split("/")
   218→    return f"{parts[-2]}/{parts[-1]}"

Now I have a thorough understanding of both the spec and the existing codebase. Here is my review.

---

## Spec Review: Workflow Generation Eval Framework

**Verdict: ISSUES FOUND**

There are several issues ranging from blocking to minor. No fundamental design flaws, but several items need fixing before implementation.

---

### Issue 1: `build_graph()` conflicts with existing workflow template (BLOCKING)

**What's wrong:** The spec (section "2. Require `build_graph()` in generated scripts") proposes changing the workflow skill's template to use a `build_graph()` function. However, the current template in `/Users/yorrickjansen/work/claude-code-plugins/dev-loop/commands/workflow.md` uses `async def main()` with graph construction inline (lines 51-65). The spec's `build_graph()` signature returns a `StateGraph` but does not accept `initial_state` -- that is constructed in the `if __name__` block. This creates a problem: generated scripts often compute `initial_state` dynamically (e.g., from `detect_available_models()`, environment variables, or CLI args). The spec does not address where `initial_state` construction goes when `build_graph()` is separated out.

**Why it matters:** If the eval framework imports `build_graph()`, the returned graph will lack the `initial_state` that may influence graph topology (e.g., conditional model selection using `HAS_CODEX`). The eval's structural assertions could miss issues that only manifest with certain initial states.

**Suggested fix:** Clarify that `build_graph()` must contain *all* graph construction logic (nodes, edges) and must not depend on `initial_state` for structural decisions. If model detection (`detect_available_models()`) affects graph topology (as it does in the current template -- see `HAS_CODEX`/`HAS_GEMINI` branching), address whether `build_graph()` should accept a `models` dict parameter or whether the eval should mock `detect_available_models()`.

---

### Issue 2: `_prompt_template` not set on `template_node` or `python_node` (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec says to add `_prompt_template` to `claude_node`, `codex_node`, `gemini_node`, and `shell_node`. It omits `template_node` (which has an interpolation template) and `python_node` (which has no template, but could be confusing in `has_node_with_prompt_containing` lookups).

**Why it matters:** `GraphInspector.has_node_with_prompt_containing()` iterates over all nodes checking `_prompt_template`. If `template_node` functions lack this attribute, `getattr(fn, '_prompt_template', None)` returns `None`, which is fine. But `template_node` does have a template string that assertions might want to inspect (e.g., checking a report node mentions certain keywords). This is a missed opportunity rather than a bug.

**Suggested fix:** Either explicitly state that `template_node` also gets `_prompt_template = template`, or document that only LLM/shell nodes have inspectable prompts.

---

### Issue 3: YAML dependency not declared (BLOCKING)

**What's wrong:** The test runner (`test_scenarios.py`) uses `yaml.safe_load` (line 167 of the spec), but PyYAML is not in the project's dependencies. The `pyproject.toml` at `/Users/yorrickjansen/work/claude-code-plugins/pyproject.toml` lists only `pyright`, `pytest`, `pytest-asyncio`, and `ruff` as dev dependencies. There are no existing uses of PyYAML in the codebase.

**Why it matters:** The test will fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'` unless PyYAML is added to the dev dependency group.

**Suggested fix:** Either add `pyyaml` to the `[dependency-groups] dev` list in `pyproject.toml`, or switch `scenario.yaml` to a simpler format (TOML via `tomllib` which is stdlib in 3.11+, or even just a plain text file since the only fields are `name` and `prompt`).

---

### Issue 4: `generate_workflow` implementation is underspecified (BLOCKING)

**What's wrong:** The spec describes `generate_workflow(prompt, repo_path) -> Path` as "Call headless Claude with the /workflow skill context and scenario prompt" but provides no implementation detail. This is the most complex and fragile part of the system. Key questions unanswered:
- How does headless Claude get the `/workflow` skill context? The skill is a Claude Code command, not something you can pass via `claude -p`.
- Does it use `claude -p` with the workflow.md content inlined? Or does it invoke Claude Code with the skill loaded?
- How does the generated `workflow.py` get extracted from Claude's output? Claude outputs JSON with a `result` field -- does the test parse that and write it to disk, or does Claude write the file directly (requiring file permissions)?
- What model/effort level should the generation call use?

**Why it matters:** This is the core mechanism of the eval. Without a clear implementation path, the implementer will have to make significant design decisions that could diverge from the spec's intent.

**Suggested fix:** Add implementation detail. The most likely approach: read `workflow.md` into a string, construct a prompt that includes the skill instructions and the scenario prompt, run `claude -p "<prompt>" --permission-mode bypassPermissions` in the repo directory, then extract/locate the generated `workflow_*.py` file from `/tmp/`. Specify this explicitly.

---

### Issue 5: `import_graph` may fail on scripts with side effects at import time (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec says `import_graph` imports `build_graph()` from the generated script. But generated scripts contain `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` at module level and `from engine import ...` -- these will execute during import. If the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` path in the generated script doesn't resolve correctly from the test's working directory, the import will fail.

**Why it matters:** The spec says "Adds the engine module to sys.path so the script's imports resolve" but the generated script *also* manipulates sys.path. These two manipulations could conflict or create import order issues.

**Suggested fix:** Document that `import_graph` must handle the path setup *before* importing the module, and that the generated script's `sys.path.insert` will use a `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` variable that may need to be resolved or mocked. Alternatively, the test could directly manipulate `sys.modules` to pre-load the engine module.

---

### Issue 6: GraphInspector references `_node_meta` values that contain model info, but assertions use meta patterns like "shell", "claude", "codex" (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The `_node_meta` dict in the engine stores the `_diagram_label` value, not a simple type string. For example, a claude node's meta is `"claude opus/high"`, not `"claude"`. A codex node's meta is `"codex default"` or `"codex o4-mini"`. The spec's assertion examples use `has_node_with_meta("shell")` and `has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex")`, which rely on substring matching. This works because `"shell"` is a substring of `"shell"` and `"claude"` is a substring of `"claude opus/high"`.

**Why it matters:** This actually works correctly, but only because the spec specifies substring matching in the docstring. Worth making this explicit in the spec text (not just the docstring) so implementers understand why `"claude"` matches `"claude opus/high"`.

**Suggested fix:** Add a brief note in the design section (not just the docstring) explaining that meta patterns use substring matching against `_diagram_label` values like `"claude opus/high"`, `"codex default"`, `"shell"`, etc.

---

### Issue 7: `has_conditional_loop` cycle detection algorithm not specified (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec describes `has_conditional_loop(meta_contains)` as "True if a conditional edge routes back to a previously-seen node (cycle)" but doesn't specify the algorithm. Detecting cycles in a graph with conditional edges requires graph traversal -- you need to determine whether any conditional edge target is an ancestor of the source in the graph. A naive implementation might just check if any conditional edge target equals any earlier node in topological order, but "earlier" is ill-defined in a graph with parallel edges and multiple paths.

**Why it matters:** An incorrect cycle detection implementation could produce false positives (reporting cycles that don't exist) or false negatives (missing actual cycles).

**Suggested fix:** Specify the algorithm. The simplest correct approach: for each conditional edge, check if any route_map target appears as a source in a chain of edges leading to the conditional edge's source node (i.e., the target is reachable from `start` and the source is reachable from the target). For the eval's purposes, a simpler heuristic may suffice: check if any conditional edge's route_map values include a node name that also appears as a source of an edge whose target chain leads to the conditional edge's source.

---

### Issue 8: No handling of non-determinism in test results (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec acknowledges LLM non-determinism in the "What this does NOT cover" section but doesn't provide guidance on handling flaky tests. Since each eval requires an LLM call, tests could pass on one run and fail on the next. The spec doesn't address retry strategies, expected failure rates, or how to distinguish "the prompt is bad" from "the LLM had an off day."

**Why it matters:** Without guidance, developers will waste time debugging flaky evals.

**Suggested fix:** Add a brief section on dealing with non-determinism: recommend running each scenario multiple times (e.g., 3 runs) when evaluating prompt changes, and consider a scenario "broken" only if it fails consistently. Optionally, add a `--runs N` flag to the test runner.

---

### Summary

| # | Issue | Severity |

Now I have a thorough understanding of both the spec and the existing codebase. Here is my review.

---

## Spec Review: Workflow Generation Eval Framework

**Verdict: ISSUES FOUND**

There are several issues ranging from blocking to minor. No fundamental design flaws, but several items need fixing before implementation.

---

### Issue 1: `build_graph()` conflicts with existing workflow template (BLOCKING)

**What's wrong:** The spec (section "2. Require `build_graph()` in generated scripts") proposes changing the workflow skill's template to use a `build_graph()` function. However, the current template in `/Users/yorrickjansen/work/claude-code-plugins/dev-loop/commands/workflow.md` uses `async def main()` with graph construction inline (lines 51-65). The spec's `build_graph()` signature returns a `StateGraph` but does not accept `initial_state` -- that is constructed in the `if __name__` block. This creates a problem: generated scripts often compute `initial_state` dynamically (e.g., from `detect_available_models()`, environment variables, or CLI args). The spec does not address where `initial_state` construction goes when `build_graph()` is separated out.

**Why it matters:** If the eval framework imports `build_graph()`, the returned graph will lack the `initial_state` that may influence graph topology (e.g., conditional model selection using `HAS_CODEX`). The eval's structural assertions could miss issues that only manifest with certain initial states.

**Suggested fix:** Clarify that `build_graph()` must contain *all* graph construction logic (nodes, edges) and must not depend on `initial_state` for structural decisions. If model detection (`detect_available_models()`) affects graph topology (as it does in the current template -- see `HAS_CODEX`/`HAS_GEMINI` branching), address whether `build_graph()` should accept a `models` dict parameter or whether the eval should mock `detect_available_models()`.

---

### Issue 2: `_prompt_template` not set on `template_node` or `python_node` (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec says to add `_prompt_template` to `claude_node`, `codex_node`, `gemini_node`, and `shell_node`. It omits `template_node` (which has an interpolation template) and `python_node` (which has no template, but could be confusing in `has_node_with_prompt_containing` lookups).

**Why it matters:** `GraphInspector.has_node_with_prompt_containing()` iterates over all nodes checking `_prompt_template`. If `template_node` functions lack this attribute, `getattr(fn, '_prompt_template', None)` returns `None`, which is fine. But `template_node` does have a template string that assertions might want to inspect (e.g., checking a report node mentions certain keywords). This is a missed opportunity rather than a bug.

**Suggested fix:** Either explicitly state that `template_node` also gets `_prompt_template = template`, or document that only LLM/shell nodes have inspectable prompts.

---

### Issue 3: YAML dependency not declared (BLOCKING)

**What's wrong:** The test runner (`test_scenarios.py`) uses `yaml.safe_load` (line 167 of the spec), but PyYAML is not in the project's dependencies. The `pyproject.toml` at `/Users/yorrickjansen/work/claude-code-plugins/pyproject.toml` lists only `pyright`, `pytest`, `pytest-asyncio`, and `ruff` as dev dependencies. There are no existing uses of PyYAML in the codebase.

**Why it matters:** The test will fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'` unless PyYAML is added to the dev dependency group.

**Suggested fix:** Either add `pyyaml` to the `[dependency-groups] dev` list in `pyproject.toml`, or switch `scenario.yaml` to a simpler format (TOML via `tomllib` which is stdlib in 3.11+, or even just a plain text file since the only fields are `name` and `prompt`).

---

### Issue 4: `generate_workflow` implementation is underspecified (BLOCKING)

**What's wrong:** The spec describes `generate_workflow(prompt, repo_path) -> Path` as "Call headless Claude with the /workflow skill context and scenario prompt" but provides no implementation detail. This is the most complex and fragile part of the system. Key questions unanswered:
- How does headless Claude get the `/workflow` skill context? The skill is a Claude Code command, not something you can pass via `claude -p`.
- Does it use `claude -p` with the workflow.md content inlined? Or does it invoke Claude Code with the skill loaded?
- How does the generated `workflow.py` get extracted from Claude's output? Claude outputs JSON with a `result` field -- does the test parse that and write it to disk, or does Claude write the file directly (requiring file permissions)?
- What model/effort level should the generation call use?

**Why it matters:** This is the core mechanism of the eval. Without a clear implementation path, the implementer will have to make significant design decisions that could diverge from the spec's intent.

**Suggested fix:** Add implementation detail. The most likely approach: read `workflow.md` into a string, construct a prompt that includes the skill instructions and the scenario prompt, run `claude -p "<prompt>" --permission-mode bypassPermissions` in the repo directory, then extract/locate the generated `workflow_*.py` file from `/tmp/`. Specify this explicitly.

---

### Issue 5: `import_graph` may fail on scripts with side effects at import time (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec says `import_graph` imports `build_graph()` from the generated script. But generated scripts contain `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` at module level and `from engine import ...` -- these will execute during import. If the `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` path in the generated script doesn't resolve correctly from the test's working directory, the import will fail.

**Why it matters:** The spec says "Adds the engine module to sys.path so the script's imports resolve" but the generated script *also* manipulates sys.path. These two manipulations could conflict or create import order issues.

**Suggested fix:** Document that `import_graph` must handle the path setup *before* importing the module, and that the generated script's `sys.path.insert` will use a `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` variable that may need to be resolved or mocked. Alternatively, the test could directly manipulate `sys.modules` to pre-load the engine module.

---

### Issue 6: GraphInspector references `_node_meta` values that contain model info, but assertions use meta patterns like "shell", "claude", "codex" (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The `_node_meta` dict in the engine stores the `_diagram_label` value, not a simple type string. For example, a claude node's meta is `"claude opus/high"`, not `"claude"`. A codex node's meta is `"codex default"` or `"codex o4-mini"`. The spec's assertion examples use `has_node_with_meta("shell")` and `has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex")`, which rely on substring matching. This works because `"shell"` is a substring of `"shell"` and `"claude"` is a substring of `"claude opus/high"`.

**Why it matters:** This actually works correctly, but only because the spec specifies substring matching in the docstring. Worth making this explicit in the spec text (not just the docstring) so implementers understand why `"claude"` matches `"claude opus/high"`.

**Suggested fix:** Add a brief note in the design section (not just the docstring) explaining that meta patterns use substring matching against `_diagram_label` values like `"claude opus/high"`, `"codex default"`, `"shell"`, etc.

---

### Issue 7: `has_conditional_loop` cycle detection algorithm not specified (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec describes `has_conditional_loop(meta_contains)` as "True if a conditional edge routes back to a previously-seen node (cycle)" but doesn't specify the algorithm. Detecting cycles in a graph with conditional edges requires graph traversal -- you need to determine whether any conditional edge target is an ancestor of the source in the graph. A naive implementation might just check if any conditional edge target equals any earlier node in topological order, but "earlier" is ill-defined in a graph with parallel edges and multiple paths.

**Why it matters:** An incorrect cycle detection implementation could produce false positives (reporting cycles that don't exist) or false negatives (missing actual cycles).

**Suggested fix:** Specify the algorithm. The simplest correct approach: for each conditional edge, check if any route_map target appears as a source in a chain of edges leading to the conditional edge's source node (i.e., the target is reachable from `start` and the source is reachable from the target). For the eval's purposes, a simpler heuristic may suffice: check if any conditional edge's route_map values include a node name that also appears as a source of an edge whose target chain leads to the conditional edge's source.

---

### Issue 8: No handling of non-determinism in test results (MINOR)

**What's wrong:** The spec acknowledges LLM non-determinism in the "What this does NOT cover" section but doesn't provide guidance on handling flaky tests. Since each eval requires an LLM call, tests could pass on one run and fail on the next. The spec doesn't address retry strategies, expected failure rates, or how to distinguish "the prompt is bad" from "the LLM had an off day."

**Why it matters:** Without guidance, developers will waste time debugging flaky evals.

**Suggested fix:** Add a brief section on dealing with non-determinism: recommend running each scenario multiple times (e.g., 3 runs) when evaluating prompt changes, and consider a scenario "broken" only if it fails consistently. Optionally, add a `--runs N` flag to the test runner.

---

### Summary

| # | Issue | Severity |
|---|-------|----------|
| 1 | `build_graph()` doesn't address `initial_state` / model detection | BLOCKING |
| 3 | PyYAML dependency not declared | BLOCKING |
| 4 | `generate_workflow` implementation underspecified | BLOCKING |
| 2 | `_prompt_template` not set on `template_node` | MINOR |
| 5 | `import_graph` path resolution with generated scripts | MINOR |
| 6 | Meta substring matching needs explicit documentation | MINOR |
| 7 | Cycle detection algorithm unspecified | MINOR |
| 8 | No guidance on handling non-determinism | MINOR |

# Workflow Generation Eval Framework

## Problem

The `/workflow` skill generates Python workflow scripts via LLM. When iterating on the skill's prompt, there's no way to systematically verify that the generated workflows make good decisions — right graph topology, appropriate model selection, correct use of parallel execution, sensitivity to repo context (CLAUDE.md instructions).

## Goal

A scenario-based eval framework that:

1. Presents a natural language task + a scaffolded repo to headless Claude
2. Claude generates a workflow.py using the `/workflow` skill
3. The generated graph is imported and inspected with Python assertions
4. No workflow execution — only structural inspection

This enables prompt iteration: change the skill, re-run evals, check if the LLM still makes good decisions.

## Design

### Engine changes

#### 1. Expose prompt templates on node functions

Add a `_prompt_template` attribute to `claude_node`, `codex_node`, `gemini_node`, and `shell_node` — same pattern as the existing `_diagram_label`. This lets assertions inspect what prompt or command each node uses.

```python
# In claude_node:
_node._prompt_template = prompt_template

# In shell_node:
_node._prompt_template = command_template
```

#### 2. Require `build_graph()` in generated scripts

Update the `/workflow` skill (commands/workflow.md) to require that generated scripts put graph construction in a `build_graph()` function. The `if __name__ == "__main__"` block calls `build_graph()` and then runs it. This makes the graph importable for inspection without execution.

```python
def build_graph():
```

A scenario-based eval framework that:

1. Presents a natural language task + a scaffolded repo to headless Claude

4. No workflow execution — only structural inspection

**Prompt pattern matching:** All `*_prompt_containing` methods use **case-insensitive substring matching** against the `_prompt_template` attribute set on node functions by the engine's node helpers.

```python
class GraphInspector:
    """Pattern-matching query interface for StateGraph inspection."""

    def __init__(self, graph: StateGraph):
        self.graph = graph

    def has_node_with_meta(self, *patterns: str) -> bool:
        """True if any node's _node_meta value contains one of the patterns.

        Example: has_node_with_meta("shell") — checks for a shell node.
        Example: has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex") — checks for either.
        """

    def get_nodes_with_meta(self, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return node names whose _node_meta value contains pattern."""

    def has_node_with_prompt_containing(self, keyword: str) -> bool:
        """True if any node's _prompt_template contains keyword (case-insensitive)."""

    def get_nodes_with_prompt_containing(self, keyword: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return node names whose _prompt_template contains keyword."""

    def has_parallel_group(self) -> bool:
        """True if the graph uses add_parallel_edges."""

    def has_parallel_group_containing(self, *meta_patterns: str) -> bool:
        """True if any parallel group's targets include nodes matching the patterns."""

    def has_conditional_loop(self, meta_contains: str | None = None) -> bool:
        """True if a conditional edge creates a cycle in the graph.

        Algorithm: for each conditional edge, check if any of its route_map
        targets is an ancestor of its source — i.e., the target appears as a
        source in any edge chain that leads to the conditional edge's source.
        Simplified approach: check if any route_map target also appears as a
        source of an edge (unconditional or parallel) earlier in the graph,
        creating a back-edge.

        If meta_contains is provided, only considers conditional edges where
        the source node's meta contains the pattern.
        """

    def node_count(self) -> int:
        """Total number of nodes in the graph."""

    def get_edge_targets(self, source_pattern: str) -> list[str]:
        """All targets reachable from nodes whose name contains source_pattern.

        Checks unconditional, conditional, and parallel edges.
        """

    def has_edge_to_end(self) -> bool:
        """True if the graph has at least one edge to END."""

    def get_model_for_node(self, node_name_pattern: str) -> str | None:
        """Return the _node_meta (model info) for the first node matching pattern."""
```

### Test runner (`test_scenarios.py`)

#### `generate_workflow`

The core mechanism. Reads the `/workflow` skill content (commands/workflow.md), constructs a prompt that includes the skill instructions and the scenario's prompt, then runs headless Claude:

```bash
claude -p "<combined_prompt>" \
    --model sonnet \
    --permission-mode bypassPermissions \
    --cwd <repo_path>
```

Claude runs with the scaffolded repo as cwd, so it picks up any CLAUDE.md in the repo. It generates a `/tmp/workflow_*.py` file. The test locates it by globbing `/tmp/workflow_*.py` (filtered by modification time to avoid collisions).

The combined prompt includes:
1. The full workflow.md skill content (so Claude knows how to generate workflows)
2. The scenario's prompt (the task to generate a workflow for)
3. An instruction to generate the workflow script (not execute it)

#### `import_graph`

Imports the generated script's `build_graph()` function and returns the graph:

1. Add the engine module's directory to `sys.path` so the script's `from engine import ...` resolves
2. Set `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` environment variable to the dev-loop plugin directory (so `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts` resolves in the generated script's path manipulation)
3. Use `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` to import the generated script
4. Call `module.build_graph(models={"claude": True, "codex": True, "gemini": True})` — pass all models as available for deterministic topology
5. Return the graph

#### Runner

```python
import tomllib

def discover_scenarios() -> list[Path]:
    """Find all scenarios/*/scenario.toml, return parent dirs."""

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "scenario_dir",
    discover_scenarios(),
    ids=lambda p: p.name,
)
def test_workflow_scenario(scenario_dir: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    with open(scenario_dir / "scenario.toml", "rb") as f:
        config = tomllib.load(f)

    repo_path = scaffold_repo(scenario_dir, tmp_path)
    workflow_path = generate_workflow(config["prompt"], repo_path)
    graph = import_graph(workflow_path)
    inspector = GraphInspector(graph)

    # Load and run scenario-specific assertions
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "assertions", scenario_dir / "assertions.py"
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    module.assert_workflow(graph, inspector)
```

### Scenarios

| # | Directory | Task | CLAUDE.md? | Key assertions |
|---|-----------|------|------------|----------------|
| 1 | `bugfix_bare` | Fix crashing function | No | test→fix loop, shell node for tests, minimal nodes, no unnecessary steps |
| 2 | `bugfix_backend_instructions` | Fix crashing function | Yes: pytest, ruff, update docs | Same loop + lint/typecheck/doc nodes from instructions |
| 3 | `feature_bare` | Add new API endpoint | No | Implement node, test node, commit node |
| 4 | `feature_backend_instructions` | Add new API endpoint | Yes: pytest, ruff, pydantic | Quality gates picked up from CLAUDE.md |
| 5 | `frontend_feature_instructions` | Add settings page | Yes: playwright, component lib | Playwright in test node prompt, appropriate models |
| 6 | `fullstack_feature_instructions` | User profile (API + UI) | Yes: pytest + playwright, docs | Both test types present, parallel where sensible |
| 7 | `refactoring_bare` | Extract class from module | No | Runs existing tests, review step, no new test creation step |

### Repo scaffolds

Each scenario's `repo/` contains a minimal but realistic project structure:

- **Python backend repos**: `src/` with a module, `tests/` with a test file, `pyproject.toml`
- **Frontend repos**: `src/components/`, `tests/e2e/`, `package.json`, `playwright.config.ts`
- **Full-stack repos**: both of the above
- **CLAUDE.md** (when present): contains specific instructions the workflow should pick up

The repos should have enough structure for the LLM to understand the project type, but stay minimal — just enough files to convey context.

### Running the evals

```bash
# Run all scenarios (slow — one LLM call per scenario)
uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -v

# Run a specific scenario
uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -k bugfix_bare -v

# Run with output capture disabled to see Claude's generation
uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -k bugfix_bare -v -s
```

These are manual evals, not CI. Run them when iterating on the `/workflow` skill prompt.

### Dealing with non-determinism

LLM outputs vary between runs. To handle this:

- **Assertions should be loose** — check for structural properties ("has a shell node", "has a conditional loop") not exact node names or counts.
- **Run multiple times when evaluating prompt changes** — run each scenario 3 times. A scenario is "broken" only if it fails consistently (2+ out of 3). A single failure may be LLM variance.
- **Save generated scripts** — when a run produces a particularly good or bad workflow, save the generated script for manual inspection. The test runner should copy generated workflow files to a `results/` directory with timestamps for later review.

### What this does NOT cover

- **Execution correctness**: We don't run the workflows. That's what `test_workflow_integration.py` already does.
- **Prompt content quality**: We check that prompts mention the right keywords (e.g., "playwright"), but not that they're well-written.

# Workflow Generation Eval Framework

## Problem

The `/workflow` skill generates Python workflow scripts via LLM. When iterating on the skill's prompt, there's no way to systematically verify that the generated workflows make good decisions — right graph topology, appropriate model selection, correct use of parallel execution, sensitivity to repo context (CLAUDE.md instructions).

## Goal

A scenario-based eval framework that:

1. Presents a natural language task + a scaffolded repo to headless Claude
2. Claude generates a workflow.py using the `/workflow` skill
3. The generated graph is imported and inspected with Python assertions
4. No workflow execution — only structural inspection

This enables prompt iteration: change the skill, re-run evals, check if the LLM still makes good decisions.

## Design

### Engine changes

#### 1. Expose prompt templates on node functions

Add a `_prompt_template` attribute to `claude_node`, `codex_node`, `gemini_node`, and `shell_node` — same pattern as the existing `_diagram_label`. This lets assertions inspect what prompt or command each node uses.

```python
# In claude_node:
_node._prompt_template = prompt_template

# In shell_node:
_node._prompt_template = command_template
```

#### 2. Require `build_graph()` in generated scripts

Update the `/workflow` skill (commands/workflow.md) to require that generated scripts put graph construction in a `build_graph()` function. The `if __name__ == "__main__"` block calls `build_graph()` and then runs it. This makes the graph importable for inspection without execution.

```python
def build_graph():
    graph = StateGraph(max_iterations=5)
    # ... add nodes, edges ...
    return graph

if __name__ == "__main__":
    graph = build_graph()
    if "--diagram" in sys.argv:
        print(graph.to_ascii())
        sys.exit(0)
    asyncio.run(graph.run(initial_state))
```

### Directory structure

```
dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/
├── helpers.py               # GraphInspector with pattern-matching query methods
├── test_scenarios.py         # Pytest runner: discover, generate, import, assert
└── scenarios/
    ├── bugfix_bare/
    │   ├── scenario.yaml     # name + prompt
    │   ├── repo/             # actual files copied to temp dir
    │   └── assertions.py     # assert_workflow(graph, inspector)
    ├── bugfix_backend_instructions/
    │   ├── scenario.yaml
    │   ├── repo/
    │   │   ├── src/...
    │   │   └── CLAUDE.md
    │   └── assertions.py
    ├── feature_bare/
    ├── feature_backend_instructions/
    ├── frontend_feature_instructions/
    ├── fullstack_feature_instructions/
    └── refactoring_bare/
```

### GraphInspector (`helpers.py`)

A query interface over the StateGraph internals. All methods operate on the graph's internal data structures (`_nodes`, `_node_meta`, `_edges`, `_conditional_edges`, `_parallel_edges`).

```python
class GraphInspector:
    """Pattern-matching query interface for StateGraph inspection.

    All query methods use substring/pattern matching to be resilient
    to LLM-chosen node names varying between runs.
    """

    def __init__(self, graph: StateGraph):
        self.graph = graph

    def has_node_with_meta(self, *patterns: str) -> bool:
        """True if any node's _node_meta value contains one of the patterns.

        Example: has_node_with_meta("shell") — checks for a shell node.
        Example: has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex") — checks for either.
        """

    def get_nodes_with_meta(self, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return node names whose _node_meta value contains pattern."""

    def has_node_with_prompt_containing(self, keyword: str) -> bool:
        """True if any node's _prompt_template contains keyword (case-insensitive).

        Uses the _prompt_template attribute added to node functions.
        """

    def get_nodes_with_prompt_containing(self, keyword: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return node names whose _prompt_template contains keyword."""

    def has_parallel_group(self) -> bool:
        """True if the graph uses add_parallel_edges."""

    def has_parallel_group_containing(self, *meta_patterns: str) -> bool:
        """True if any parallel group's targets include nodes matching the patterns."""

    def has_conditional_loop(self, meta_contains: str | None = None) -> bool:
        """True if a conditional edge routes back to a previously-seen node (cycle).

        If meta_contains is provided, only considers loops where the source node's
        meta contains the pattern (e.g., meta_contains='shell' for test-fix loops).
        """

    def node_count(self) -> int:
        """Total number of nodes in the graph."""

    def get_edge_targets(self, source_pattern: str) -> list[str]:
        """All targets reachable from nodes whose name contains source_pattern.

        Checks unconditional, conditional, and parallel edges.
        """

    def has_edge_to_end(self) -> bool:
        """True if the graph has at least one edge to END."""

    def get_model_for_node(self, node_name_pattern: str) -> str | None:
        """Return the _node_meta (model info) for the first node matching pattern."""
```

### Test runner (`test_scenarios.py`)

```python
def discover_scenarios() -> list[Path]:
    """Find all scenarios/*/scenario.yaml, return parent dirs."""

def scaffold_repo(scenario_dir: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Copy scenario's repo/ tree to tmp_path, run git init."""

def generate_workflow(prompt: str, repo_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Call headless Claude with the /workflow skill context and scenario prompt.

    Returns path to the generated workflow.py file.
    Claude runs with the repo_path as cwd so it picks up any CLAUDE.md.
    """

def import_graph(workflow_path: Path) -> StateGraph:
    """Import build_graph() from the generated script, return the graph.

    Adds the engine module to sys.path so the script's imports resolve.
    """

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "scenario_dir",
    discover_scenarios(),
    ids=lambda p: p.name,
)
def test_workflow_scenario(scenario_dir: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    config = yaml.safe_load((scenario_dir / "scenario.yaml").read_text())
    repo_path = scaffold_repo(scenario_dir, tmp_path)
    workflow_path = generate_workflow(config["prompt"], repo_path)
    graph = import_graph(workflow_path)
    inspector = GraphInspector(graph)

    # Load and run scenario-specific assertions
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "assertions", scenario_dir / "assertions.py"
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    module.assert_workflow(graph, inspector)
```

### Scenario format

#### `scenario.yaml`

```yaml
name: Bug fix on bare repo
prompt: |
  Fix the calculate_average function in src/mathlib.py —
  it crashes on empty lists with a ZeroDivisionError
```

Minimal — just name and prompt. Repo context (including CLAUDE.md if any) lives as actual files in the `repo/` directory.

#### `assertions.py`

```python
def assert_workflow(graph, h):
    """Assertions for: bug fix on a bare repo (no CLAUDE.md)."""

    # Should have a test runner node
    assert h.has_node_with_meta("shell"), "needs a shell node to run tests"

    # Should have a fix node using an LLM
    assert h.has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex"), "needs an LLM node to fix the bug"

    # Test failure should loop back to fix
    assert h.has_conditional_loop(meta_contains="shell"), "test→fix loop expected"

    # Should terminate
    assert h.has_edge_to_end(), "graph must terminate"

    # Bare repo — should NOT have doc update or lint steps
    assert not h.has_node_with_prompt_containing("doc"), "no doc step expected on bare repo"
```

### Scenarios

| # | Directory | Task | CLAUDE.md? | Key assertions |
|---|-----------|------|------------|----------------|
| 1 | `bugfix_bare` | Fix crashing function | No | test→fix loop, shell node for tests, minimal nodes, no unnecessary steps |
| 2 | `bugfix_backend_instructions` | Fix crashing function | Yes: pytest, ruff, update docs | Same loop + lint/typecheck/doc nodes from instructions |
| 3 | `feature_bare` | Add new API endpoint | No | Implement node, test node, commit node |
| 4 | `feature_backend_instructions` | Add new API endpoint | Yes: pytest, ruff, pydantic | Quality gates picked up from CLAUDE.md |
| 5 | `frontend_feature_instructions` | Add settings page | Yes: playwright, component lib | Playwright in test node prompt, appropriate models |
| 6 | `fullstack_feature_instructions` | User profile (API + UI) | Yes: pytest + playwright, docs | Both test types present, parallel where sensible |
| 7 | `refactoring_bare` | Extract class from module | No | Runs existing tests, review step, no new test creation step |

### Repo scaffolds

Each scenario's `repo/` contains a minimal but realistic project structure:

- **Python backend repos**: `src/` with a module, `tests/` with a test file, `pyproject.toml`
- **Frontend repos**: `src/components/`, `tests/e2e/`, `package.json`, `playwright.config.ts`
- **Full-stack repos**: both of the above
- **CLAUDE.md** (when present): contains specific instructions the workflow should pick up

The repos should have enough structure for the LLM to understand the project type, but stay minimal — just enough files to convey context.

### Running the evals

```bash
# Run all scenarios (slow — one LLM call per scenario)
uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -v

# Run a specific scenario
uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -k bugfix_bare -v

# Run with output capture disabled to see Claude's generation
uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -k bugfix_bare -v -s
```

These are manual evals, not CI. Run them when iterating on the `/workflow` skill prompt.

### What this does NOT cover

- **Execution correctness**: We don't run the workflows. That's what `test_workflow_integration.py` already does.
- **Prompt content quality**: We check that prompts mention the right keywords (e.g., "playwright"), but not that they're well-written.
- **Non-determinism**: LLM outputs vary. Assertions should be loose enough to accept reasonable variation but tight enough to catch bad decisions.

1→# Workflow Generation Eval Framework
     2→
     3→## Problem
     4→
     5→The `/workflow` skill generates Python workflow scripts via LLM. When iterating on the skill's prompt, there's no way to systematically verify that the generated workflows make good decisions — right graph topology, appropriate model selection, correct use of parallel execution, sensitivity to repo context (CLAUDE.md instructions).
     6→
     7→## Goal
     8→
     9→A scenario-based eval framework that:
    10→
    11→1. Presents a natural language task + a scaffolded repo to headless Claude
    12→2. Claude generates a workflow.py using the `/workflow` skill
    13→3. The generated graph is imported and inspected with Python assertions
    14→4. No workflow execution — only structural inspection
    15→
    16→This enables prompt iteration: change the skill, re-run evals, check if the LLM still makes good decisions.
    17→
    18→## Design
    19→
    20→### Engine changes
    21→
    22→#### 1. Expose prompt templates on node functions
    23→
    24→Add a `_prompt_template` attribute to `claude_node`, `codex_node`, `gemini_node`, `shell_node`, and `template_node` — same pattern as the existing `_diagram_label`. This lets assertions inspect what prompt or command each node uses.
    25→
    26→```python
    27→# In claude_node:
    28→_node._prompt_template = prompt_template
    29→
    30→# In shell_node:
    31→_node._prompt_template = command_template
    32→
    33→# In template_node:
    34→_node._prompt_template = template
    35→```
    36→
    37→`python_node` does not get `_prompt_template` since it wraps arbitrary functions with no template string.
    38→
    39→#### 2. Require `build_graph()` in generated scripts
    40→
    41→Update the `/workflow` skill (commands/workflow.md) to require that generated scripts put graph construction in a `build_graph()` function. This makes the graph importable for inspection without execution.
    42→
    43→`build_graph()` accepts an optional `models` parameter (defaulting to `detect_available_models()`) so that callers can control model availability for deterministic graph topology:
    44→
    45→```python
    46→def build_graph(models: dict[str, bool] | None = None) -> StateGraph:
    47→    if models is None:
    48→        models = detect_available_models()
    49→    HAS_CODEX = models["codex"]
    50→    HAS_GEMINI = models["gemini"]
    51→
    52→    graph = StateGraph(max_iterations=5)
    53→    # ... add nodes, edges, using HAS_CODEX/HAS_GEMINI for node selection ...
    54→    return graph
    55→
    56→if __name__ == "__main__":
    57→    graph = build_graph()
    58→    if "--diagram" in sys.argv:
    59→        print(graph.to_ascii())
    60→        sys.exit(0)
    61→    initial_state = {"work_dir": os.getcwd(), ...}
    62→    asyncio.run(graph.run(initial_state))
    63→```
    64→
    65→All graph topology decisions (node types, edges, parallel groups) must happen inside `build_graph()`. The `if __name__` block only handles `initial_state` construction and execution.
    66→
    67→### Directory structure
    68→
    69→```
    70→dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/
    71→├── helpers.py               # GraphInspector with pattern-matching query methods
    72→├── test_scenarios.py         # Pytest runner: discover, generate, import, assert
    73→└── scenarios/
    74→    ├── bugfix_bare/
    75→    │   ├── scenario.toml     # name + prompt
    76→    │   ├── repo/             # actual files copied to temp dir
    77→    │   └── assertions.py     # assert_workflow(graph, inspector)
    78→    ├── bugfix_backend_instructions/
    79→    │   ├── scenario.toml
    80→    │   ├── repo/
    81→    │   │   ├── src/...
    82→    │   │   └── CLAUDE.md
    83→    │   └── assertions.py
    84→    ├── feature_bare/
    85→    ├── feature_backend_instructions/
    86→    ├── frontend_feature_instructions/
    87→    ├── fullstack_feature_instructions/
    88→    └── refactoring_bare/
    89→```
    90→
    91→### Scenario format
    92→
    93→#### `scenario.toml`
    94→
    95→Uses TOML (stdlib `tomllib` since Python 3.11, no external dependency):
    96→
    97→```toml
    98→name = "Bug fix on bare repo"
    99→prompt = """
   100→Fix the calculate_average function in src/mathlib.py —
   101→it crashes on empty lists with a ZeroDivisionError
   102→"""
   103→```
   104→
   105→Minimal — just name and prompt. Repo context (including CLAUDE.md if any) lives as actual files in the `repo/` directory.
   106→
   107→#### `assertions.py`
   108→
   109→```python
   110→def assert_workflow(graph, h):
   111→    """Assertions for: bug fix on a bare repo (no CLAUDE.md)."""
   112→
   113→    # Should have a test runner node
   114→    assert h.has_node_with_meta("shell"), "needs a shell node to run tests"
   115→
   116→    # Should have a fix node using an LLM
   117→    assert h.has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex"), "needs an LLM node to fix the bug"
   118→
   119→    # Test failure should loop back to fix
   120→    assert h.has_conditional_loop(meta_contains="shell"), "test→fix loop expected"
   121→
   122→    # Should terminate
   123→    assert h.has_edge_to_end(), "graph must terminate"
   124→
   125→    # Bare repo — should NOT have doc update or lint steps
   126→    assert not h.has_node_with_prompt_containing("doc"), "no doc step expected on bare repo"
   127→```
   128→
   129→### GraphInspector (`helpers.py`)
   130→
   131→A query interface over the StateGraph internals. All methods operate on the graph's internal data structures (`_nodes`, `_node_meta`, `_edges`, `_conditional_edges`, `_parallel_edges`).
   132→
   133→**Meta pattern matching:** All `*_meta` methods use **substring matching** against the `_diagram_label` values stored in `_node_meta`. For example, `"claude"` matches `"claude opus/high"`, `"shell"` matches `"shell"`, `"codex"` matches `"codex default"`. This makes assertions resilient to model/effort variations.
   134→
   135→**Prompt pattern matching:** All `*_prompt_containing` methods use **case-insensitive substring matching** against the `_prompt_template` attribute set on node functions by the engine's node helpers.
   136→
   137→```python
   138→class GraphInspector:
   139→    """Pattern-matching query interface for StateGraph inspection."""
   140→
   141→    def __init__(self, graph: StateGraph):
   142→        self.graph = graph
   143→
   144→    def has_node_with_meta(self, *patterns: str) -> bool:
   145→        """True if any node's _node_meta value contains one of the patterns.
   146→
   147→        Example: has_node_with_meta("shell") — checks for a shell node.
   148→        Example: has_node_with_meta("claude", "codex") — checks for either.
   149→        """
   150→
   151→    def get_nodes_with_meta(self, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
   152→        """Return node names whose _node_meta value contains pattern."""
   153→
   154→    def has_node_with_prompt_containing(self, keyword: str) -> bool:
   155→        """True if any node's _prompt_template contains keyword (case-insensitive)."""
   156→
   157→    def get_nodes_with_prompt_containing(self, keyword: str) -> list[str]:
   158→        """Return node names whose _prompt_template contains keyword."""
   159→
   160→    def has_parallel_group(self) -> bool:
   161→        """True if the graph uses add_parallel_edges."""
   162→
   163→    def has_parallel_group_containing(self, *meta_patterns: str) -> bool:
   164→        """True if any parallel group's targets include nodes matching the patterns."""
   165→
   166→    def has_conditional_loop(self, meta_contains: str | None = None) -> bool:
   167→        """True if a conditional edge creates a cycle in the graph.
   168→
   169→        Algorithm: for each conditional edge, check if any of its route_map
   170→        targets is an ancestor of its source — i.e., the target appears as a
   171→        source in any edge chain that leads to the conditional edge's source.
   172→        Simplified approach: check if any route_map target also appears as a
   173→        source of an edge (unconditional or parallel) earlier in the graph,
   174→        creating a back-edge.
   175→
   176→        If meta_contains is provided, only considers conditional edges where
   177→        the source node's meta contains the pattern.
   178→        """
   179→
   180→    def node_count(self) -> int:
   181→        """Total number of nodes in the graph."""
   182→
   183→    def get_edge_targets(self, source_pattern: str) -> list[str]:
   184→        """All targets reachable from nodes whose name contains source_pattern.
   185→
   186→        Checks unconditional, conditional, and parallel edges.
   187→        """
   188→
   189→    def has_edge_to_end(self) -> bool:
   190→        """True if the graph has at least one edge to END."""
   191→
   192→    def get_model_for_node(self, node_name_pattern: str) -> str | None:
   193→        """Return the _node_meta (model info) for the first node matching pattern."""
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Test runner (`test_scenarios.py`)
   197→
   198→#### `generate_workflow`
   199→
   200→The core mechanism. Reads the `/workflow` skill content (commands/workflow.md), constructs a prompt that includes the skill instructions and the scenario's prompt, then runs headless Claude:
   201→
   202→```bash
   203→claude -p "<combined_prompt>" \
   204→    --model sonnet \
   205→    --permission-mode bypassPermissions \
   206→    --cwd <repo_path>
   207→```
   208→
   209→Claude runs with the scaffolded repo as cwd, so it picks up any CLAUDE.md in the repo. It generates a `/tmp/workflow_*.py` file. The test locates it by globbing `/tmp/workflow_*.py` (filtered by modification time to avoid collisions).
   210→
   211→The combined prompt includes:
   212→1. The full workflow.md skill content (so Claude knows how to generate workflows)
   213→2. The scenario's prompt (the task to generate a workflow for)
   214→3. An instruction to generate the workflow script (not execute it)
   215→
   216→#### `import_graph`
   217→
   218→Imports the generated script's `build_graph()` function and returns the graph:
   219→
   220→1. Add the engine module's directory to `sys.path` so the script's `from engine import ...` resolves
   221→2. Set `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` environment variable to the dev-loop plugin directory (so `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts` resolves in the generated script's path manipulation)
   222→3. Use `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` to import the generated script
   223→4. Call `module.build_graph(models={"claude": True, "codex": True, "gemini": True})` — pass all models as available for deterministic topology
   224→5. Return the graph
   225→
   226→#### Runner
   227→
   228→```python
   229→import tomllib
   230→
   231→def discover_scenarios() -> list[Path]:
   232→    """Find all scenarios/*/scenario.toml, return parent dirs."""
   233→
   234→@pytest.mark.parametrize(
   235→    "scenario_dir",
   236→    discover_scenarios(),
   237→    ids=lambda p: p.name,
   238→)
   239→def test_workflow_scenario(scenario_dir: Path, tmp_path: Path):
   240→    with open(scenario_dir / "scenario.toml", "rb") as f:
   241→        config = tomllib.load(f)
   242→
   243→    repo_path = scaffold_repo(scenario_dir, tmp_path)
   244→    workflow_path = generate_workflow(config["prompt"], repo_path)
   245→    graph = import_graph(workflow_path)
   246→    inspector = GraphInspector(graph)
   247→
   248→    # Load and run scenario-specific assertions
   249→    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
   250→        "assertions", scenario_dir / "assertions.py"
   251→    )
   252→    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
   253→    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
   254→    module.assert_workflow(graph, inspector)
   255→```
   256→
   257→### Scenarios
   258→
   259→| # | Directory | Task | CLAUDE.md? | Key assertions |
   260→|---|-----------|------|------------|----------------|
   261→| 1 | `bugfix_bare` | Fix crashing function | No | test→fix loop, shell node for tests, minimal nodes, no unnecessary steps |
   262→| 2 | `bugfix_backend_instructions` | Fix crashing function | Yes: pytest, ruff, update docs | Same loop + lint/typecheck/doc nodes from instructions |
   263→| 3 | `feature_bare` | Add new API endpoint | No | Implement node, test node, commit node |
   264→| 4 | `feature_backend_instructions` | Add new API endpoint | Yes: pytest, ruff, pydantic | Quality gates picked up from CLAUDE.md |
   265→| 5 | `frontend_feature_instructions` | Add settings page | Yes: playwright, component lib | Playwright in test node prompt, appropriate models |
   266→| 6 | `fullstack_feature_instructions` | User profile (API + UI) | Yes: pytest + playwright, docs | Both test types present, parallel where sensible |
   267→| 7 | `refactoring_bare` | Extract class from module | No | Runs existing tests, review step, no new test creation step |
   268→
   269→### Repo scaffolds
   270→
   271→Each scenario's `repo/` contains a minimal but realistic project structure:
   272→
   273→- **Python backend repos**: `src/` with a module, `tests/` with a test file, `pyproject.toml`
   274→- **Frontend repos**: `src/components/`, `tests/e2e/`, `package.json`, `playwright.config.ts`
   275→- **Full-stack repos**: both of the above
   276→- **CLAUDE.md** (when present): contains specific instructions the workflow should pick up
   277→
   278→The repos should have enough structure for the LLM to understand the project type, but stay minimal — just enough files to convey context.
   279→
   280→### Running the evals
   281→
   282→```bash
   283→# Run all scenarios (slow — one LLM call per scenario)
   284→uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -v
   285→
   286→# Run a specific scenario
   287→uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -k bugfix_bare -v
   288→
   289→# Run with output capture disabled to see Claude's generation
   290→uv run pytest dev-loop/tests/workflow_eval/test_scenarios.py -k bugfix_bare -v -s
   291→```
   292→
   293→These are manual evals, not CI. Run them when iterating on the `/workflow` skill prompt.
   294→
   295→### Dealing with non-determinism
   296→
   297→LLM outputs vary between runs. To handle this:
   298→
   299→- **Assertions should be loose** — check for structural properties ("has a shell node", "has a conditional loop") not exact node names or counts.
   300→- **Run multiple times when evaluating prompt changes** — run each scenario 3 times. A scenario is "broken" only if it fails consistently (2+ out of 3). A single failure may be LLM variance.
   301→- **Save generated scripts** — when a run produces a particularly good or bad workflow, save the generated script for manual inspection. The test runner should copy generated workflow files to a `results/` directory with timestamps for later review.
   302→
   303→### What this does NOT cover
   304→
   305→- **Execution correctness**: We don't run the workflows. That's what `test_workflow_integration.py` already does.
   306→- **Prompt content quality**: We check that prompts mention the right keywords (e.g., "playwright"), but not that they're well-written.
   307→

1→#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
     2→# /// script
     3→# requires-python = ">=3.10"
     4→# dependencies = ["mermaid-ascii"]
     5→# ///
     6→"""Lightweight async graph execution engine for orchestrating headless AI coding agents.
     7→
     8→Provides a LangGraph-inspired StateGraph builder with support for:
     9→- Async node execution
    10→- Conditional edges with router functions
    11→- Parallel execution groups
    12→- Loop detection with max_iterations safety valve
    13→- Event callbacks for observability
    14→"""
    15→
    16→from __future__ import annotations
    17→
    18→import asyncio
    19→import inspect
    20→import json
    21→import os
    22→import shutil
    23→import sys
    24→import time
    25→from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
    26→from dataclasses import dataclass
    27→from pathlib import Path
    28→
    29→# Type aliases
    30→State = dict[str, str]
    31→NodeFn = Callable[[State], Awaitable[State]]
    32→RouterFn = Callable[[State], str]
    33→
    34→
    35→class _SafeFormatMap(dict[str, str]):
    36→    """Dict subclass that returns empty string for missing keys in format_map.
    37→
    38→    This makes template interpolation safe in loops — on the first pass,
    39→    ``{previous_findings}`` resolves to ``""`` instead of raising KeyError.
    40→    """
    41→
    42→    def __missing__(self, key: str) -> str:
    43→        return ""
    44→
    45→
    46→def _format_elapsed(seconds: float) -> str:
    47→    minutes, secs = divmod(int(seconds), 60)
    48→    return f"{minutes}m{secs:02d}s"
    49→
    50→
    51→class _EndSentinel:
    52→    """Sentinel object representing the end of graph execution."""
    53→
    54→    def __repr__(self) -> str:
    55→        return "END"
    56→
    57→    def __str__(self) -> str:
    58→        return "END"
    59→
    60→    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
    61→        return isinstance(other, _EndSentinel)
    62→
    63→    def __hash__(self) -> int:
    64→        return hash("__END__")
    65→
    66→
    67→END = _EndSentinel()
    68→
    69→
    70→class MaxIterationsExceeded(Exception):
    71→    """Raised when the graph exceeds the maximum number of loop iterations."""
    72→
    73→
    74→@dataclass
    75→class _Edge:
    76→    source: str
    77→    target: str | _EndSentinel
    78→
    79→
    80→@dataclass
    81→class _ConditionalEdge:
    82→    source: str
    83→    router: RouterFn
    84→    route_map: dict[str, str | _EndSentinel]
    85→
    86→
    87→class StateGraph:
    88→    """Graph builder and async executor for workflow orchestration."""
    89→
    90→    def __init__(self, max_iterations: int = 5, cwd: Path | None = None) -> None:
    91→        self.max_iterations = max_iterations
    92→        self.cwd = cwd
    93→        self._nodes: dict[str, NodeFn] = {}
    94→        self._node_meta: dict[str, str] = {}  # name -> label for diagram
    95→        self._edges: list[_Edge] = []
    96→        self._conditional_edges: list[_ConditionalEdge] = []
    97→        self._parallel_edges: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    98→
    99→        # Event callbacks
   100→        self._on_node_start: list[Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]] = []
   101→        self._on_node_end: list[Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]] = []
   102→        self._on_error: list[Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]] = []
   103→
   104→    def add_node(self, name: str, fn: NodeFn) -> None:
   105→        """Register a named node with its async callable."""
   106→        self._nodes[name] = fn
   107→        # Extract diagram label from node metadata if set by node helpers
   108→        label = getattr(fn, "_diagram_label", None)
   109→        if label:
   110→            self._node_meta[name] = label
   111→
   112→    def add_edge(self, source: str, target: str | _EndSentinel) -> None:
   113→        """Add an unconditional edge from source to target."""
   114→        self._edges.append(_Edge(source, target))
   115→
   116→    def add_conditional_edges(self, source: str, router: RouterFn, route_map: dict[str, str | _EndSentinel]) -> None:
   117→        """Add a conditional edge with a router function."""
   118→        self._conditional_edges.append(_ConditionalEdge(source, router, route_map))
   119→
   120→    def add_parallel_edges(self, source: str, targets: list[str]) -> None:
   121→        """Add parallel edges from source to multiple targets."""
   122→        self._parallel_edges[source] = targets
   123→
   124→    def on_node_start(self, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]:
   125→        """Decorator to register a node_start callback."""
   126→        self._on_node_start.append(fn)
   127→        return fn
   128→
   129→    def on_node_end(self, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]:
   130→        """Decorator to register a node_end callback."""
   131→        self._on_node_end.append(fn)
   132→        return fn
   133→
   134→    def on_error(self, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]:
   135→        """Decorator to register an error callback."""
   136→        self._on_error.append(fn)
   137→        return fn
   138→
   139→    def _get_next_node(self, current: str) -> str | None:
   140→        """Get next node after current. Returns None if END reached.
   141→
   142→        Note: Conditional and parallel edges are handled separately in run().
   143→        This method only resolves unconditional edges.
   144→        """
   145→        for edge in self._edges:
   146→            if edge.source == current:
   147→                if edge.target == END or isinstance(edge.target, _EndSentinel):
   148→                    return None
   149→                if isinstance(edge.target, str):
   150→                    return edge.target
   151→
   152→        return None
   153→
   154→    def _get_conditional_target(self, current: str, state: State) -> str | _EndSentinel | None:
   155→        """Evaluate conditional edge router and return target."""
   156→        for ce in self._conditional_edges:
   157→            if ce.source == current:
   158→                label = ce.router(state)
   159→                target = ce.route_map.get(label)
   160→                if target is None:
   161→                    raise ValueError(f"Router for '{current}' returned unknown label '{label}'")
   162→                return target
   163→        return None
   164→
   165→    def _diagram_id(self, name: str) -> str:
   166→        """Return a diagram-friendly node ID, embedding metadata if present."""
   167→        meta = self._node_meta.get(name)
   168→        if meta:
   169→            # Encode metadata into the ID: "implement" → "implement:codex"
   170→            return f"{name}:{meta}"
   171→        return name
   172→
   173→    def to_mermaid(self) -> str:
   174→        """Generate a Mermaid flowchart string from the graph structure.
   175→
   176→        Nodes with metadata (model, effort, etc.) get annotated IDs like
   177→        ``implement:codex_default`` so the diagram shows what runs each step.
   178→        """
   179→        lines: list[str] = ["graph TD"]
   180→        did = self._diagram_id
   181→
   182→        # Unconditional edges
   183→        for edge in self._edges:
   184→            target = "END" if isinstance(edge.target, _EndSentinel) else did(edge.target)
   185→            lines.append(f"    {did(edge.source)} --> {target}")
   186→
   187→        # Conditional edges (with labels)
   188→        for ce in self._conditional_edges:
   189→            for label, target in ce.route_map.items():
   190→                target_name = "END" if isinstance(target, _EndSentinel) else did(target)
   191→                lines.append(f"    {did(ce.source)} -->|{label}| {target_name}")
   192→
   193→        # Parallel edges
   194→        for source, targets in self._parallel_edges.items():
   195→            for t in targets:
   196→                lines.append(f"    {did(source)} --> {did(t)}")
   197→
   198→        return "\n".join(lines)
   199→
   200→    def to_ascii(self) -> str:
